activeExperiment.name: R4-Y / R4-Z Labor Coherence Superbatch
activeExperiment.description: Canonical 24m and restructuring 36m experiments across original A/B/C and held-out D/E/F seeds, comparing control / production / settlement / realized / hybrid labor-demand rules.

causalChain: Labor demand / retained workforce exceeds realized sustainable payroll
Eventual liquidation and firm exit propagate unemployment
Inactive estates strand physical and financial resources
Supply and demand weaken further, amplifying collapse

researchTimeline.result: Long-run collapse reproduced under controlled baseline.
Labor matching, voluntary consumption cuts, and single-factor credit explanations narrowed or rejected as primary roots.
Exit propagation identified as a major late-stage unemployment amplifier; generic root search closed.
Entrant credit timing and startup-finance defects confirmed, but aggregate employment impact remained secondary.
Estate stranding and accounting representation defects confirmed; tax-feedback root hypothesis falsified.
Restructure-vs-liquidate architecture shown to be economically material; supply relief becomes a complement after restructuring.
Detached former-worker claims exist, but do not explain the restructuring arrears penalty; current-worker arrears dominate.
Post-restructure payroll coverage remains severely inadequate and restructuring recurs across original and held-out seeds.
Currently testing labor-demand coherence rules across 120 regimes.

notes: Diagnostic-only results are kept separate from canonical production repairs.
Observer instrumentation must not alter simulation state.
A PASS on accounting identity is not treated as proof of economic realism.
Dashboard data should be updated whenever a diagnostic closure materially changes the causal frontier.
